cycles.summary: Authored the nda-reviewer skill to the standard Lawcal legal-tech package: SKILL.md (English), SKILL_HE.md (Hebrew mirror), two references (nda-review-checklist, standard-clauses), an offline stdlib-only NDA clause flagger, metadata.json, evidence.json, and this log. The skill is general and cross-jurisdiction (NOT Israeli-specific) and reviews for one-sided terms, term/survival length, missing carve-outs, and IP-assignment traps. Its central discipline is reading a clause by what it does, not the document title, and routing enforceability questions to counsel. Ran the script self-check (--selftest: OK).

changes.detail: Authored SKILL.md: deal context, mutuality/balance tests, definition scope, the five standard carve-outs, term/survival/return, the IP/licence/feedback trap catalogue, prioritized redline, anti-overreach discipline, examples, gotchas, reference links, troubleshooting.
Added SKILL_HE.md: Hebrew RTL mirror of the instructions, examples, gotchas, and reference links.
Added references/nda-review-checklist.md (end-to-end review pass) and references/standard-clauses.md (model balanced language + red-flag patterns for each common clause).
Added metadata.json (author, version 1.0.0, category, bilingual tags + display name/description, supported agents).
Added evidence.json documenting 6 claims sourced to the method references, WIPO trade-secret guidance, and the local script self-check.
Verified scripts/nda_scanner.py --selftest passes on python3.11 (stdlib only, no network).

deferrals.reason: Whether a specific clause (non-compete, liquidated damages, choice of law) is enforceable is jurisdiction-specific and requires local counsel. The skill deliberately flags such clauses and routes the validity question rather than opining, to avoid giving wrong jurisdiction-specific advice.

Deciding whether a clause is fair (vs merely present) requires reading the clause and knowing the deal direction and leverage. The scanner deliberately stops at pattern-based flagging and defers the fairness call to the human/agent.
